subtitle: Lesson 18 · Azure Networking

eyebrow: The six fields of every NSG rule

code:
az network nsg rule create \
  --nsg-name nsg-web --name Allow-HTTPS \
  --priority 100 --access Allow --protocol Tcp \
  --destination-port-ranges 443 \
  --source-address-prefixes Internet

az network nsg rule create \
  --nsg-name nsg-web --name Allow-SSH-Admin \
  --priority 110 --access Allow --protocol Tcp \
  --destination-port-ranges 22 \
  --source-address-prefixes 203.0.113.5/32
caption: HTTPS open to the internet at priority 100; SSH open only to one admin IP at priority 110.

eyebrow: Attaching the NSG to a subnet
code:
az network vnet subnet update \
  --resource-group rg-network-demo \
  --vnet-name vnet-prod \
  --name snet-web \
  --network-security-group nsg-web
caption: Inbound traffic hits the subnet NSG first, then any NIC-level NSG; both must allow it.
